channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Attention Misses Visual Risk: Risk-Adaptive Steering for Multimodal Safety Alignment
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a failure mode in multimodal safety where models miss safety-critical regions in images.
  • Proposes Multimodal Risk-Adaptive Steering (MoRAS) to improve visual attention for risk assessment and enable risk-adaptive refusals at inference time.
  • Shows reduced overhead and improved generalization against diverse multimodal jailbreaks across benchmarks and multiple multimodal LLM backbones.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jonghyun Park', 'Minhyuk Seo', 'Chaewon Yeo', 'Jonghyun Choi']
  • Tags: ['multimodal-jailbreaking', 'safety-alignment', 'inference-time-defense', 'risk-assessment', 'visual-attention']

item.title: SALMUBench: A Benchmark for Sensitive Association-Level Multimodal Unlearning
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SALMUBench to evaluate multimodal machine unlearning at the sensitive association (persona–attribute) level.
  • Uses a synthetic persona-attribute association dataset to create a compromised vs. clean contrastively-trained multimodal encoder setup.
  • Proposes structured holdouts (identity and association) to measure both forgetting effectiveness and collateral damage/over-generalization.
  • Provides dataset, models, evaluation scripts, and leaderboards for benchmarking unlearning methods.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Cai Selvas-Sala', 'Lei Kang', 'Lluis Gomez']
  • Tags: ['machine unlearning', 'privacy/memorization', 'multimodal (contrastive encoders)', 'benchmarking/evaluation']

item.title: Gaussian Shannon: High-Precision Diffusion Model Watermarking Based on Communication
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Gaussian Shannon, a diffusion-model watermarking framework that embeds watermark payloads into the initial Gaussian noise treated as a noisy communication channel.
  • Introduces defenses against two interference types (local bit flips and global stochastic distortions) using error-correcting codes plus majority voting for reliable end-to-end recovery.
  • Claims bit-exact (lossless) watermark payload recovery for offline verification/licensing instruction use, with robust tracing under multiple perturbations across Stable Diffusion variants.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yi Zhang', 'Hongbo Huang', 'Liang-Jie Zhang']
  • Tags: ['AI watermarking', 'diffusion models', 'robustness/error-correction', 'content provenance/rights attribution', 'steganography/communication-channel coding']

item.title: IP-Bench: Benchmark for Image Protection Methods in Image-to-Video Generation Scenarios
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes IP-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating image protection methods specifically in image-to-video (I2V) generation misuse settings.
  • Evaluates 6 image protection methods against 5 state-of-the-art I2V models.
  • Includes systematic robustness testing using two robustness attack strategies and studies cross-model/cross-modality transferability.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xiaofeng Li', 'Leyi Sheng', 'Zhen Sun', 'Zongmin Zhang', 'Jiaheng Wei', 'Xinlei He']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'data/content protection', 'image-to-video (I2V) misuse', 'robustness evaluation', 'adversarial attacks']

item.title: R-PGA: Robust Physical Adversarial Camouflage Generation via Relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes R-PGA, a framework for generating physically robust adversarial camouflage by mapping adversarial textures onto 3D objects for autonomous driving threats.
  • Uses relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting for photo-realistic reconstruction and disentangled rendering attributes to handle illumination/material changes.
  • Adds Hard Physical Configuration Mining to reduce worst-case loss peaks and flatten the optimization landscape for robustness across viewing and physical configurations.
  • Introduces a hybrid rendering pipeline combining relightable 3DGS foreground rendering with image-translation relighting for background plausibility.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Tianrui Lou', 'Siyuan Liang', 'Jiawei Liang', 'Yuze Gao', 'Xiaochun Cao']
  • Tags: ['Physical adversarial attacks', 'Adversarial camouflage', 'Robustness to physical transformations', '3D Gaussian Splatting']

item.title: Face2Parts: Exploring Coarse-to-Fine Inter-Regional Facial Dependencies for Generalized Deepfake Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Face2Parts, a coarse-to-fine facial-region feature approach for generalized deepfake (forgery) detection.
  • Analyzes prior forensic methods and builds a hybrid model using hierarchical feature representation with channel-attention and deep triplet learning.
  • Evaluates across multiple deepfake benchmarks and settings (intra-, inter-dataset, inter-manipulation), reporting strong AUC performance.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kutub Uddin', 'Nusrat Tasnim', 'Byung Tae Oh']
  • Tags: ['deepfake-detection', 'multimedia-forensics', 'facial-region-analysis', 'generalization-evaluation']

item.title: The Hidden Puppet Master: Predicting Human Belief Change in Manipulative LLM Dialogues
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies manipulative LLM dialogues that steer users via hidden incentives.
  • Introduces a taxonomy and dataset (PUPPET) linking manipulative incentives to measured human belief shifts.
  • Finds a disconnect between manipulation-detection performance and actual magnitude of users’ belief change.
  • Proposes and evaluates a belief-shift prediction task for AI social safety.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jocelyn Shen', 'Amina Luvsanchultem', 'Jessica Kim', 'Kynnedy Smith', 'Valdemar Danry', 'Kantwon Rogers', 'Hae Won Park', 'Maarten Sap', 'Cynthia Breazeal']
  • Tags: ['LLM manipulation', 'Human belief steering', 'AI social safety', 'Evaluation dataset', 'Red teaming/behavioral testing']

item.title: CLASP: Defending Hybrid Large Language Models Against Hidden State Poisoning Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CLASP (Classifier Against State Poisoning) to detect Hidden State Poisoning Attacks (HiSPAs) targeting state space models like Mamba and hybrid LLM architectures.
  • Frames HiSPA mitigation as token-level binary classification using patterns in Mamba block output embeddings, with an XGBoost-based detector.
  • Evaluates on resume corpus with controlled adversarial injections and reports high token- and document-level detection performance, including generalization to unseen attack patterns.
  • Designed as a lightweight, independent front-line defense with low latency and modest VRAM requirements.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alexandre Le Mercier', 'Thomas Demeester', 'Chris Develder']
  • Tags: ['AI Security', 'Poisoning Attacks', 'Attack Detection', 'State Space Models (SSM)']

item.title: H-Node Attack and Defense in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies “Hallucination Nodes” (H-Nodes) in transformer hidden states via a logistic regression probe with AUC ~0.90.
  • Introduces a white-box adversarial attack that amplifies hallucination-related hidden-state dimensions at inference using forward hooks, with low visibility to a defender.
  • Proposes adaptive Hallucination Noise Cancellation (ANC) defenses that suppress excessive H-Node activations via confidence-weighted cancellation and iterative re-ranking, improving robustness while minimally impacting perplexity and MMLU.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Eric Yocam', 'Varghese Vaidyan', 'Yong Wang']
  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'adversarial attacks', 'hallucination manipulation', 'defense/robustness']

item.title: Shape and Substance: Dual-Layer Side-Channel Attacks on Local Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes and evaluates dual-layer side-channel attacks against on-device vision-language models caused by dynamic high-resolution preprocessing (e.g., AnyRes).
  • Tier 1 fingerprints input geometry using execution-time/workload-dependent variations observable via unprivileged OS metrics.
  • Tier 2 leverages Last-Level Cache contention profiling to disambiguate semantics within identical geometries (dense vs sparse content), enabling privacy-sensitive context inference.
  • Analyzes mitigations (e.g., constant-work padding) and trade-offs, with engineering recommendations for secure Edge AI deployments.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Eyal Hadad', 'Mordechai Guri']
  • Tags: ['Side-Channel Attacks', 'Privacy Leakage', 'Edge AI Security', 'Vision-Language Models', 'Cache Timing Attacks']

item.title: A Channel-Triggered Backdoor Attack on Wireless Semantic Image Reconstruction
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a channel-triggered backdoor attack (CT-BA) for wireless semantic communications, targeting semantic image reconstruction/symbol reconstruction in JSCC/semantic communication systems.
  • Uses wireless channel characteristics (e.g., channel gain under different fading distributions, channel noise power) as natural activation triggers instead of explicit input-level triggers.
  • Evaluates across multiple JSCC architectures and datasets, reporting near-perfect attack success rate while maintaining stealth.
  • Discusses potential defense mechanisms against channel-triggered backdoor attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jialin Wan (Sherman)', 'Jinglong Shen (Sherman)', 'Nan Cheng (Sherman)', 'Zhisheng Yin (Sherman)', 'Yiliang Liu (Sherman)', 'Wenchao Xu (Sherman)', 'Xuemin (Sherman)', 'Shen']
  • Tags: ['Backdoor attacks', 'Wireless semantic communications', 'Channel-triggered attacks', 'Semantic image reconstruction', 'JSCC']

item.title: Does Audio Deepfake Detection Generalize?
item.description:
Summary

  • Re-implements and uniformly evaluates existing audio deepfake/spoof detection architectures to determine what factors drive success.
  • Identifies feature choices (e.g., cqtspec/logspec over melspec) that substantially improve detection performance.
  • Assesses out-of-distribution generalization using a new found-audio dataset with both real and deepfake celebrity/politician clips.
  • Finds related methods degrade severely on real-world data, suggesting limited robustness beyond benchmark settings.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Nicolas M. M\\"uller', 'Pavel Czempin', 'Franziska Dieckmann', 'Adam Froghyar', 'Konstantin B\\"ottinger']
  • Tags: ['deepfake detection', 'audio security', 'generalization/robustness', 'spoofing detection', 'evaluation/benchmark']

item.title: Neural Uncertainty Principle: A Unified View of Adversarial Fragility and LLM Hallucination
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a unified theory (Neural Uncertainty Principle) linking adversarial fragility in vision to LLM hallucination via a shared geometric/uncertainty bound.
  • Introduces a “single-backward probe” to measure an input-gradient correlation channel and predict hallucination/fragility risk before generation.
  • Develops mitigation methods ConjMask (masking high-contribution input components) and LogitReg (logit-side regularization), aiming to improve robustness without adversarial training.
  • Presents decoding-free risk signaling for LLM hallucination detection and prompt selection based on probe measurements.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Dong-Xiao Zhang', 'Hu Lou', 'Jun-Jie Zhang', 'Jun Zhu', 'Deyu Meng']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'hallucination risk', 'uncertainty principles', 'gradient-based probing', 'defense via masking/regularization']

item.title: Is the Hard-Label Cryptanalytic Model Extraction Really Polynomial?
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies model extraction attacks in the hard-label (label-only) setting for ReLU DNNs via oracle access.
  • Challenges the polynomial-time claim of prior work by showing how certain near-constant neurons can block the attack unless their parameters are recovered.
  • Proposes a new attack method, cross-layer extraction, to overcome depth-related query complexity limits.
  • Primary focus is on attack feasibility, complexity, and adversarial extraction effectiveness under realistic output constraints.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Akira Ito', 'Takayuki Miura', 'Yosuke Todo']
  • Tags: ['Model Extraction', 'Hard-Label Attacks', 'Cryptanalysis of Neural Networks', 'Query Complexity']

item.title: Defending Against Knowledge Poisoning Attacks During Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies the vulnerability of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to knowledge poisoning attacks (specifically PoisonedRAG).
  • Proposes defense methods (FilterRAG, ML-FilterRAG) that identify and filter adversarial/poisoned knowledge passages from the retrieval corpus.
  • Evaluates defenses on benchmark datasets, showing mitigation effectiveness with limited performance loss compared to standard RAG.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kennedy Edemacu', 'Vinay M. Shashidhar', 'Micheal Tuape', 'Dan Abudu', 'Beakcheol Jang', 'Jong Wook Kim']
  • Tags: ['knowledge-poisoning', 'RAG security', 'retrieval defense', 'adversarial text filtering']

item.title: Privacy-Accuracy Trade-offs in High-Dimensional LASSO under Perturbation Mechanisms
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes privacy-preserving sparse linear regression with LASSO in high-dimensional settings under differential privacy via output perturbation and objective perturbation.
  • Uses approximate message passing (AMP) to characterize typical estimator behavior under random design and added privacy noise.
  • Quantifies privacy using typical-case measures such as on-average KL divergence (distinguishability of neighboring datasets) and studies privacy-accuracy trade-offs.
  • Finds that sparsity/regularization level strongly affects privacy-accuracy behavior and that objective perturbation can show non-monotonic or destabilizing effects with excessive noise.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ayaka Sakata', 'Haruka Tanzawa']
  • Tags: ['differential privacy', 'privacy-accuracy tradeoff', 'sparse learning (LASSO)', 'privacy mechanisms', 'typical-case analysis']

item.title: PEANUT: Perturbations by Eigenvalue Alignment for Attacking GNNs Under Topology-Driven Message Passing
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PEANUT, a gradient-free, restricted black-box evasion attack on Graph Neural Networks that injects virtual nodes to exploit vulnerabilities tied to adjacency/Laplacian topology message passing.
  • Operates at inference time (evasion) and modifies the effective graph connectivity rather than requiring feature knowledge for injected nodes.
  • Demonstrates that even zero-feature injected nodes can significantly deteriorate GNN performance, emphasizing connectivity-driven attack impact.
  • Extensive experiments across multiple real-world graph tasks to validate effectiveness.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Bhavya Kohli', 'Biplab Sikdar']
  • Tags: ['evasion attack', 'graph neural networks', 'black-box attack', 'topology perturbation', 'node injection']

item.title: Are LLM-Enhanced Graph Neural Networks Robust against Poisoning Attacks?
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a robustness assessment framework for LLM-enhanced GNNs under poisoning attacks manipulating both graph structure and textual node attributes.
  • Evaluates 24 victim models across combinations of LLM/LM-based feature enhancers and GNN backbones using structural and textual poisoning attacks at multiple granularities.
  • Finds LLM-enhanced GNNs are more robust (higher accuracy, lower relative drop) than a shallow embedding baseline under various poisoning settings.
  • Includes analysis of robustness factors and proposes a graph purification defense; also outlines offensive/defensive future directions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuhang Ma', 'Jie Wang', 'Zheng Yan']
  • Tags: ['poisoning attacks', 'graph neural networks', 'LLM-enhanced models', 'adversarial robustness', 'defense (graph purification)']

item.title: Adversarial-Robust Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection via Joint Information Retention
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ARTA, an adversarially robust framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection.
  • Uses a joint min-max training setup with a sparsity-constrained mask generator that applies minimal temporal perturbations to maximally increase anomaly scores.
  • Trains the detector to remain stable under these structured adversarial perturbations and uses the learned masks as explanations of sensitivity to corruptions.
  • Evaluates on the TSB-AD benchmark, reporting improved robustness and graceful degradation under noise compared to baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hadi Hojjati', 'Narges Armanfard']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'anomaly detection', 'min-max optimization', 'time-series', 'input perturbation']

item.title: Why Safety Probes Catch Liars But Miss Fanatics
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies activation-based safety probes for detecting deceptively aligned AI.
  • Identifies a blind spot where probes fail on coherent misalignment (models that rationalize harmful behavior as virtuous).
  • Proves limits: no polynomial-time probe can reliably detect misalignment under sufficiently complex belief structures (PRF-like triggers).
  • Demonstrates empirically that two RLHF-trained models—one explicitly hostile and one coherently misaligned via rationalizations—show very different probe detectability (liar detected; fanatic evades).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kristiyan Haralambiev']
  • Tags: ['AI safety probing', 'deceptive alignment detection', 'adversarial evasion', 'internal activation analysis', 'misalignment evaluation']

item.title: Insider Knowledge: How Much Can RAG Systems Gain from Evaluation Secrets?
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies evaluation-security vulnerabilities in RAG systems when LLM-judge feedback is used for optimization.
  • Demonstrates that leaking/predicting evaluation elements (e.g., prompt templates, gold nuggets) enables near-perfect evaluation scores via metric overfitting/circularity.
  • Performs comparative experiments modifying nugget-based systems (e.g., Crucible) to exploit judge-based evaluation.
  • Recommends blind evaluation settings and methodological diversity to reduce faulty measurements.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Laura Dietz', 'Bryan Li', 'Eugene Yang', 'Dawn Lawrie', 'William Walden', 'James Mayfield']
  • Tags: ['RAG', 'LLM-judge evaluation', 'Metric overfitting', 'Evaluation leakage', 'Adversarial evaluation/circularity']

item.title: ProbGuard: Probabilistic Runtime Monitoring for LLM Agent Safety
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ProbGuard, a proactive runtime monitoring framework for LLM agents that predicts future safety violations before they occur.
  • Models agent behavior using symbolic-state abstraction and a learned discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) from execution traces.
  • At runtime, estimates probability of reaching unsafe states and triggers interventions when risk exceeds a threshold; includes semantic validity constraints and PAC-style guarantees.
  • Evaluated on safety-critical domains (autonomous driving and embodied household agents) showing earlier warnings and reduced unsafe behavior.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Haoyu Wang', 'Christopher M. Poskitt', 'Jiali Wei', 'Jun Sun']
  • Tags: ['runtime monitoring', 'LLM agents safety', 'probabilistic risk prediction', 'guardrails/intervention']

item.title: Knowdit: Agentic Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection with Auditing Knowledge Summarization
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents Knowdit, an agentic framework to detect vulnerabilities in smart contracts by leveraging a knowledge graph built from historical human audit reports.
  • Uses an iterative loop including specification generation, harness synthesis, fuzz execution, and reflection to identify recurring DeFi-specific vulnerability patterns (via “DeFi semantics”).
  • Evaluated on Code4rena projects with reported ground-truth vulnerabilities and also applied to real-world projects to find previously unknown issues.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ziqiao Kong', 'Wanxu Xia', 'Chong Wang', 'Yi Lu', 'Pan Li', 'Shaohua Li', 'Zong Cao', 'Yang Liu']
  • Tags: ['smart-contract security', 'vulnerability detection', 'agentic auditing', 'fuzzing', 'Code4rena']

item.title: Clawed and Dangerous: Can We Trust Open Agentic Systems?
item.description:
Summary

  • Systematizes security challenges of open agentic (LLM-planning + tools/memory/privilege) systems under persistent uncertainty.
  • Surveys literature spanning attacks, benchmarks, defenses, and audits; proposes a six-dimensional security taxonomy and an evaluation scorecard.
  • Identifies gaps in deployment controls, operational governance, persistent-memory integrity, and capability revocation; outlines a secure-by-construction doctrine.
  • Primary focus is on identifying and addressing vulnerabilities/attack surfaces in agentic systems.

Paper Type

  • Survey/Review

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shiping Chen', 'Qin Wang', 'Guangsheng Yu', 'Xu Wang', 'Liming Zhu']
  • Tags: ['AI agent security', 'adversarial attacks & governance', 'jailbreak/prompt & tool-output threats', 'robustness & defensive engineering', 'security benchmarks & audits']

item.title: CANGuard: A Spatio-Temporal CNN-GRU-Attention Hybrid Architecture for Intrusion Detection in In-Vehicle CAN Networks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CANGuard, a CNN-GRU-attention spatio-temporal deep learning model to detect intrusion attacks on in-vehicle CAN bus networks.
  • Targets security threats in IoV communications, specifically DoS and spoofing attacks.
  • Trains and evaluates on CICIoV2024 dataset and compares against prior methods; includes ablation and SHAP interpretability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rakib Hossain Sajib', 'Md. Rokon Mia', 'Prodip Kumar Sarker', 'Abdullah Al Noman', 'Md Arifur Rahman']
  • Tags: ['intrusion-detection', 'CAN bus security', 'DoS and spoofing detection', 'spatio-temporal ML']

item.title: BeSafe-Bench: Unveiling Behavioral Safety Risks of Situated Agents in Functional Environments
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces BeSafe-Bench to evaluate behavioral safety risks of situated agents in functional (Web/Mobile/Embodied) environments.
  • Builds an instruction/task space augmented with nine categories of safety-critical risks and evaluates using rule-based checks plus LLM-as-judge reasoning.
  • Finds agents often fail both task success and safety adherence, with cases where high performance correlates with severe safety violations.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuxuan Li', 'Yi Lin', 'Peng Wang', 'Shiming Liu', 'Xuetao Wei']
  • Tags: ['AI Safety Benchmark', 'Behavioral Safety', 'Situated Agents', 'LLM-as-a-judge Evaluation', 'Multimodal/Embodied Agents']
